acceptance.output_evidence:
RECORDED FOR L9, NO VERDICT.

1. WHICH BOUNDARY THE REPLAY COULD NOT CROSS, AND WHAT FWD-2's EXERCISED BAR THEREFORE STILL LACKS. The boundary this replay could not cross is AUTHENTICATION ITSELF on the real path: no mechanism exists (found by this worker, without a human) to mint a valid RS256 JWT the portal-authorizer would accept. This is NOT the same gap as at hand-off -- CloudFront is now live, and this cell's own live probes prove the edge+authorizer chain genuinely refuses an unauthenticated or malformed-credential caller for all 11 declared routes, with a message shape (401 'Invalid or expired token' vs API Gateway's generic 401 'Unauthorized' on the CloudFront-bypass control) that discriminates 'no token' from 'wrong door' from 'bad token' -- three DIFFERENT refusal reasons, never conflated. What FWD-2's EXERCISED bar still lacks: an AUTHENTICATED six-swap run all the way through CloudFront -> edge validator -> API Gateway authorizer -> handler, as one continuous real request. Everything downstream of the authorizer (the six-swap authorization proof, arms b-e) is exercised on the POST-AUTHORIZER plane instead -- a REAL invocation of the REAL deployed handler code with the REAL header contract, but not preceded by a REAL JWT verification in the same request. The gap this leaves is narrow and specific: this replay cannot show that a request carrying a VALID JWT for principal X, with X's claims correctly mapped by the REAL edge validator and REAL authorizer into the exact header/context shape this cell assumed, reaches the handler unchanged. It assumes that mapping is faithful because it read index.mjs's own code; it did not observe the mapping happen end-to-end on a live, authenticated request.

2. WHICH ROUTE'S REFUSAL CAME FROM THE EDGE, WHICH FROM THE AUTHORIZER, WHICH FROM THE HANDLER -- AND WHETHER THAT LAYERING IS WHAT THE DESIGN INTENDED. Three distinct refusal SOURCES were measured, not assumed, across the two planes: (i) EDGE (CloudFront/auth-validator-edge): not independently isolated by this replay -- every real-path probe that reached the authorizer had already passed the edge Lambda (a request that failed there would not reach API Gateway at all, and this cell measured no case of that, since it never held origin-appropriate-but-edge-invalid input). (ii) AUTHORIZER (opal-portal-authorizer, naqxlm): measured DIRECTLY and repeatedly -- the missing-header case (401 'Missing or invalid Authorization header'), the malformed/forged-JWT case (401 'Invalid or expired token', a DIFFERENT message proving verification was attempted), and the origin-bypass case (401 'Unauthorized', API Gateway's OWN generic message when the authorizer's isOriginVerified() check fails before JWT verification even starts) are three DISTINCT refusal shapes from what is architecturally ONE authorizer function taking three different early-exit branches. (iii) HANDLER (via _authz.Enforcer.guard(), on the POST-AUTHORIZER plane): measured directly for every GUARDED route -- FIRM_BINDING, OBJECT_NOT_COVERED, EMPTY_GRANT, KEY_REFUSED are all handler-layer (Enforcer) refusal codes, never edge or authorizer codes, and none of them ever appeared in a real-path probe (which never got past the authorizer to reach a handler at all, by construction of an unauthenticated/malformed probe). WHETHER THAT LAYERING IS WHAT THE DESIGN INTENDED: for the 5 GUARDED routes, yes as far as this replay can show -- three independent layers (edge presence, authorizer identity+origin, handler authorization+entitlement) each refuse on a DIFFERENT question, which is defense in depth rather than one gate wearing three hats. For the 6 UNGUARDED routes (row S9's 3 plus this cell's newly-filed 3, row W1-S10), the layering is INCOMPLETE by design-gap, not by design: the edge and authorizer layers still refuse an unauthenticated caller identically (verified on the real path -- the boundary probes above did not distinguish guarded from unguarded routes, because none of them got past the authorizer), but ONCE past the authorizer, an authenticated caller reaching one of these 6 handlers meets NO THIRD LAYER -- the handler either trusts whatever resolved_scope it is handed (directory, performance) or refuses everything regardless of identity for an unrelated reason (ycharts-generate's consent gate, export-status's capabilities-only dispatch) or has no identity field to check at all (narrative). Whether three independent layers were the INTENDED design for the whole surface, or whether the wrapper amendment intended EVERY route to reach a fourth (handler) layer and 6 of 11 simply have not been migrated yet, is not something this cell's instrumentation can answer -- it is a decomposition-sequencing question the issuer amendment itself names for the 3 disclosed routes and this cell extends the same open question to the 3 newly measured ones.

mutant.description: The load-bearing claim across every guarded route is that the six-swap refusal is REAL discrimination, not a vacuous always-refuse. Reused, not reinvented: this cell's own six_swaps() driver asserts BOTH the authorized request is served (served.ok) AND each of the six swaps is refused (out.ok is False, distinct codes per kind) -- a handler that refused EVERYTHING (the shape a broken guard would take) would fail the authorized_ok assertion, and a handler that served EVERYTHING would fail all six swap assertions. The ycharts-generate route's own VACUOUS-BOTH-REFUSED finding is the empirical instance of exactly this discriminator firing: this cell measured (not assumed) that route's authorized and swapped requests are IDENTICAL, and reported it as VACUOUS rather than folding it into the guarded-route pass count.
mutant.expected: A guarded route's authorized request must serve (ok=true) AND every one of its six swaps must refuse (ok=false); a route that fails either half is not counted as GUARDED-AND-DISCRIMINATING.
mutant.observed: 5 of 5 reauthorization-testable routes (status x3 sharing one mechanism, export submit, export download) served their authorized request AND refused every swap, each with a REFUSAL CODE (OBJECT_NOT_COVERED, FIRM_BINDING, EMPTY_GRANT, KEY_REFUSED across the various arms) rather than a generic failure -- discriminating codes, not a blanket denial. The ycharts-generate route's own vacuous-refusal shape was CAUGHT and REPORTED as such (authorized_live_call == swapped_live_call == 'REFUSED', identical_refusal=true) rather than silently counted as a discriminating pass, which is the mutant-detection property applied to a REAL route rather than an injected one.
